General election

Campaign

Following the May Republican runoff, both nominees quickly pivoted to the general election.[319] Paxton's victory was welcomed by Democrats who viewed him as a weaker opponent, leading several nonpartisan forecasters to rate the race as more competitive.[227] Talarico adopted a more aggressive strategy, highlighting allegations that led to Paxton's impeachment by fellow Republicans.[320] Paxton portrayed Talarico as an extremist, emphasizing culture war issues and gender, while criticizing his statement that "God is non-binary" and questioning his masculinity.[321][322] Paxton also repeatedly called Talarico a vegan, claiming "you can't get elected as a vegan in Texas," prompting Talarico to release photos and videos of himself eating meat and other non-vegan foods at campaign events.[323] In June, Talarico criticized the Attorney General's office over its handling of a child sexual abuse case involving former attorney Adam Hoffman during Paxton's tenure.[324] After a mistrial, Hoffman received a plea deal critics called "unusually lenient" and an "Epstein-style sweetheart deal," as it did not require him to register as a sex offender.[325] Talarico and John Cornyn had previously aired campaign ads criticizing Paxton over the case.[326][327]

Both Talarico and Paxton have faced challenges unifying their parties after the primaries, with limited support from former rivals exposing weaknesses in their coalitions.[328] Talarico has sought to bolster support among Black voters after defeating Jasmine Crockett, who skipped the state Democratic convention and declined to commit to campaigning for him, raising concerns about Black turnout.[329] Paxton has struggled with moderate Republicans who backed John Cornyn, with polls showing some Cornyn voters supporting Talarico.[328] Cornyn has also declined to fundraise for Paxton, instead focusing on competitive Senate races in other states.[330]

In part to rally support behind candidates such as Paxton, the Republican Party hosted its first ever midterm national convention in Dallas on September 9 and 10.[331] After the midterm convention, Paxton said in a private conversation that the convention had a negative effect for the Republican Party.[332]

On July 16, the Paxton and Talarico campaigns announced negotiations for up to three general election debates.[333] If held, they would mark Paxton's first debates since becoming a statewide elected official.[334][335][336] By September, Talarico had accepted a fourth invitation to a debate as Paxton had remained noncommittal, but insisted that they were still negotiating and expected to participate in at least one debate before the election.[337] Responding to a challenge issued by Talarico to appear on the channel,[338] a fifth debate invitation was issued by Fox News.[339] In early October, president Donald Trump and several other prominent Republicans called on Paxton to debate Talarico.[340] As of October 18, 2026[update], Paxton has not accepted an invitation to a single debate with Talarico.[341]

Election administration

The election is taking place amidst a broader push by the Trump administration to restrict mail-in voting, although these efforts are currently mired in court proceedings.[342] On September 1, commissioners in Tarrant County, Texas's third-largest county, voted to close roughly a third of its polling locations, a year after cutting early-voting sites in half, citing cost savings at low-turnout locations. Critics warned the closures could increase travel times and suppress turnout.[343] Later that month, Votebeat reported that the Department of Public Safety had failed to distribute nearly 200,000 voter registrations to counties over the course of the past year due to a technical error, sparking a bipartisan outcry.[344] By the beginning of October, the reported size of the backlog had neared 600,000 registrations.[345] The backlog was sent to counties all at once, with many of the state's urban counties receiving tens of thousands one month before early voting was set to begin.[344] The state agreed to reimburse counties for the overtime pay incurred processing the glut of applications.[346] Observers and election experts highlighted the debacle as an example of the difficulties involved in registering to vote in Texas, one of the only states in the country to not offer universal online voter registration.[347]

Fundraising

Talarico has considerably outraised Paxton throughout the campaign. Due to the high national profile of the race, both candidates, especially Talarico have received significant contributions from voters across the country. Within Texas, Talarico's donation base is concentrated in his home city of Austin and the state's other urban areas, while Paxton's is in Dallas.[439] Despite Talarico's individual fundraising advantage, however, leading into the fall campaign season, and particularly after the Republican National Convention in Dallas, Paxton has seen a massive infusion of political action committee and political party spending on his behalf to try to buoy his sagging polling numbers.[440] The Senate Leadership Fund alone committed over $100 million to support Paxton, far exceeding Talarico's individual fundraising numbers, though a remarkably high investment to defend a seat in a state Republicans have not lost in over 30 years.[441] Elon Musk also donated $10 million to Lone Star Liberty PAC, a group supporting Ken Paxton.[442] The Supreme Court over the summer additionally cleared the way for political parties themselves to freely coordinate advertising spending with candidates at the candidates' reduced rate, handing Republicans a monetary advantage across the country due to the Democratic Party lagging behind the Republicans in party fundraising.[443] The Talarico campaign raised $64 million in the third quarter of 2026, the largest quarterly total by a U.S. Senate candidate ever, surpassing the $57 million record that had been set by Jaime Harrison in the 2020 South Carolina senate race.[444][445]
